summary: You produced a well-structured, technically sound preliminary mission design for ZYZZsat, addressing all space-segment requirements with genuine STK evidence and hand calculations. Your introduction, launch/orbit/ground-control rationale and conclusions are strong. To reach the top rubric levels, attach your STK software files, add numbered figure/table captions, replace Wikipedia and bare-URL references with proper citations, and fix the technical and editorial slips noted below.
next_steps: Attach your STK scenario files (or export packages) in an appendix so your access and orbit results can be verified, and number all figures and tables (e.g. Figure 1, Table 1) with captions referenced in the text.
Replace the Wikipedia citation and bare URLs with full references (authors, titles, year, access dates) in a consistent style, and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list.

Proofread carefully: correct 'undesirable' in the orbit altitude discussion, complete the broken drag-sail sentence, rewrite the contradictory EOL/graveyard-orbit paragraph for your LEO satellite, and fix the J2/RAAN explanation (precession ∝ cos i, zero at i = 90°; SSO uses ~98° retrograde inclination).

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your introduction clearly covers the primary mission (fluid-lensing reef imaging), the rationale with cited bleaching statistics, the single-spacecraft justification, and users such as CSIRO and BOM. Referencing is appropriate. To reach 9-10, deepen the discussion distinguishing the operator from customers/users and their respective needs and responsibilities.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (8/10). All major requirements are covered: Vega E from Guiana with rationale, a full COE table for your SSO, no manoeuvres until EOL, ground-station selection logic, STK access analysis quantifying contact frequency, and a 5-year duration with drag-sail EOL. Minor technical slips (J2 explanation, 'undesirable' typo) and the missing STK software files keep you from 9-10.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (7/10). Your conclusions are specific and traceable to evidence, including honest caveats about Vega E availability and alternatives. To strengthen, expand slightly to summarise the EOL plan and communications findings, so the conclusion fully reflects all evidence in the report.
criteria.C4: Adequate (5/10). Your structure is clear with headings and an executive summary, but figures and tables lack numbered captions, the bibliography uses bare URLs and cites Wikipedia (explicitly disallowed), and typos/incomplete sentences persist (e.g. 'a Earth observation', the broken drag-sail sentence). Consistent formatting and polished referencing are required for the Accomplished level.
